study.title: Revelation 5 The sealed book and the dignity of the Lamb
study.overview: John sees a sealed book in the right hand of the one on the throne, and the scene shows that God's plan for history cannot be opened by any creature. The pain of the seer is interrupted when an elder announces the victory of the Lion of the tribe of Judah, identified shortly thereafter as the Lamb who was killed and is now alive. As he takes the book, heaven responds with increasing worship: first the living beings and the elders, then an uncountable multitude of angels, and finally all creation. The chapter concludes with the entire heavenly court confessing that praise, honor, and power belong to the throne and the Lamb forever.

outline.title: The sealed book and the inability of every creature
outline.explanation: John sees the book written on both sides and sealed with seven seals in God's right hand. A strong angel asks who is worthy to open it, but no one in heaven, on earth or under the earth can do so. John's sorrow shows that without anyone worthy, God's purposes remain closed to mankind.

outline.title: The Lion Who Is Lamb and the New Song
outline.explanation: An elder comforts John by announcing that the Lion of the tribe of Judah has won and can open the book. When John looks, however, he sees a Lamb as dead, but standing, with signs of spiritual power and fullness. This Lamb takes the book and receives worship; the new song explains why he is worthy of it: his death and his blood bought a people from all the nations and made him kings and priests for God.

outline.title: Universal Worship of the Lamb and to what is on the throne
outline.explanation: The scene extends to an immeasurable crowd of angels who proclaim the dignity of the Lamb. Then all creation joins the acclamation addressed to what is on the throne and to the Lamb. The chapter ends with living beings saying "Amen" and the elders prostrating in worship.

study.context: The chapter resumes the scene of the throne previously begun and deepens it, showing that the decrees of God, symbolized by the book, belong to his sovereign government. The given notes understand the book as an image of the divine purpose for history and the church. The text also uses images of the Old Testament, such as the lion of Judah and the root of David, to point to the person of Christ.
study.theology: The centrality of the chapter is in Christ's exclusive dignity to reveal and execute God's purposes. The contrast between the Lion and the Lamb teaches that the victory of the Messiah comes through sacrifice, not by brute force. Worship is Christological and also theocentric: praise to the Lamb does not rival the praise of the Father, but manifests it in perfect unity. The new song highlights redemption as a substitutive and universal work in scope: peoples, languages, tribes, and nations are attained by the blood of the Lamb. Moreover, the identity of the redeemed people includes priestly and royal vocation, indicating service, access to God and future participation in the divine reign. The fact that all creation worship shows that the work of Christ has a cosmic and eschatological dimension.

scholarViews.insight: The book symbolizes God's plan for history, written in a complete and sealed way until the Lamb opens it.
The book represents the counsels and decrees of God, and only Christ, as Mediator, receives the charge to open it.
The closing of the chapter highlights the final worship of the entire creation, which attributes to the throne and to the Lamb praise, honor, glory and power.

questions: Why does John weep before hearing that the Lamb has won, and what does this reveal about our dependence on Christ to understand the action of God?
How does the union between the Lion and the Lamb correct human expectations about power, victory and spiritual leadership?
How should the identity of kings and priests shape the daily life of whom was redeemed by the blood of Christ?
study.practice: Read this chapter as an invitation to trust and worship. When it seems that history is closed or unanswered, remember that Christ is the only one worthy to open what God has decreed. Instead of seeking control, practice surrender; instead of isolating, unite with the song of heaven with gratitude for redemption. Serve God as one called to the priesthood, interceding for others and living worthy of the people who were bought by the blood of the Lamb.
study.uncertainty: The notes provided feature some interpretive readings and symbolic allusions, but do not authorize additional historical details about date, location, recipients, or exact circumstances of the sealed book. There is also textual variation mentioned by Adam Clarke in verse 14, but the biblical text provided here follows the form received in the question. The interpretations of the precise meaning of the seven stamps, the seven horns and the seven eyes remain inferential, even if consistent with the notes.
